description.text: Ettore Ferrari was born in Rome on 25 March 1845 into an artistic family; his father was a painter. He became a professor at the Accademia di San Luca, served as a deputy in the Italian Parliament, and rose to become Grand Master of the Grande Oriente d'Italia, the main Masonic body in Italy.

Ferrari’s sculptural legacy includes the rough draft plans for the Victor Emmanuel II Monument in 1884, a statue of Ovid erected in Constanţa in 1887 and later duplicated for Sulmona in 1925, a bronze statue of Giuseppe Garibaldi in Pisa (1892), and the controversial Monument to Giordano Bruno in Rome’s Campo de’ Fiori.

curiosities.text: He was initiated into the Masonic lodge "Rienzi" in Rome in 1881 and became its Grand Master in 1892.
From 1904 to 1917 he served as Grand Master of the Grand Orient of Italy.
Ferrari was a professor at the Accademia di San Luca, influencing a generation of Italian artists.
His 1887 statue of Ovid for Constanţa was later duplicated in 1925 for Ovid’s birthplace, Sulmona.
In 1892 he created a bronze statue of Giuseppe Garibaldi that now stands in Pisa’s Garibaldi Square.
He collaborated with Pio Piacentini in 1884 to draft the plans for the Victor Emmanuel II Monument, a key symbol of Italy’s unification.
Ferrari sculpted the Monument to Giordano Bruno in Rome’s Campo de’ Fiori, a work that sparked controversy.
